summary: Money Message is a double-extortion operation first reported in March-April 2023 with a C++ Windows encryptor and a Linux 'esxi' build. The one detailed public intrusion (Sophos X-Ops, August 2023) began with a single-factor VPN login, then disabled Defender through Group Policy, used PsExec to enable RDP, dumped the SAM with Impacket, and exfiltrated finance/HR shares with MEGAsync before encryption. No 2024-2026 TTP reporting was found, and current activity is unverified.
uniqueTraits: Windows Defender real-time protection disabled domain-wide through a GPO
Encryptor config embeds domain credentials to encrypt network shares; files are not renamed and the note is C:\money_message.log
Separate Linux 'esxi' payload that deletes virtual disks on ESXi hosts

sources.title: Step by step through the Money Message ransomware

chain.procedure: Logs in through the victim's VPN, which used single-factor authentication, with valid credentials.
chain.noAtomicReason: No local atomic reproduces VPN logon with valid credentials (local T1133 test is a Chrome VPN-extension check). Validate with VPN/IdP logon analytics and an MFA-coverage review.

chain.techniqueName: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification
chain.procedure: Creates or modifies a Group Policy Object to turn off Windows Defender real-time protection across the domain.

atomics.testName: LockBit Black - Modify Group policy settings -cmd
atomics.note: Modifies Group Policy settings from cmd (LockBit-style GPO abuse) (local ART T1484.001 #1)

atomics.testName: Tamper with Windows Defender Command Prompt
atomics.note: Tampers with Windows Defender settings locally; covers the end-state of the GPO change (local ART T1685 #20)

chain.procedure: PsExec runs a batch script on remote hosts to enable the RDP port.

atomics.testName: Use PsExec to execute a command on a remote host
atomics.note: PsExec runs a command on a remote host (local ART T1569.002 #2)

atomics.testName: Copy and Execute File with PsExec
atomics.note: Copies and executes a file with PsExec (local ART T1021.002 #3)

chain.procedure: After RDP is enabled, the attacker moves between hosts over RDP.

atomics.note: Enables RDP through the fDenyTSConnections registry value (the batch-script effect) (local ART T1112 #70)
RDP connection to a remote host (local ART T1021.001 #1)

chain.techniqueName: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
chain.procedure: Impacket secretsdump.py retrieves the SAM registry hive.

atomics.testName: Registry dump of SAM, creds, and secrets
atomics.note: reg save of SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hives, the same artefacts secretsdump reads remotely (local ART T1003.002 #1)

chain.procedure: A compromised account browses Finance, Payroll, SalesReport and HR folders on a file server to collect data for extortion.

atomics.testName: Copy a sensitive File over Administrative share with copy
atomics.note: Copies a sensitive file over an administrative share (local ART T1039 #1)

chain.techniqueName: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
chain.procedure: MEGAsync uploads the collected data to MEGA.

atomics.testName: Exfiltrate data with rclone to cloud Storage - Mega (Windows)
atomics.note: Exfiltrates to MEGA with rclone; same destination, different client (local ART T1567.002 #1)

chain.procedure: windows.exe (C++, ChaCha + ECDH) uses an embedded JSON config (excluded folders, service/process kill list, domain credentials) to encrypt local files and network shares without renaming them, then writes C:\money_message.log.

atomics.note: Drops a ransom note; exercises note-creation detections without encrypting (local ART T1486 #5)

chain.procedure: On ESXi the operator copies the Linux 'esxi' build to /tmp, sets it to 777 and runs it; the payload deletes the virtual hard disks.

atomics.note: Deletes ESXi VM snapshots (T1485); the closest local ESXi destructive test to deleting virtual disks (local ART T1485 #5)

atomics.testName: ESXi - vim-cmd Used to Power Off VMs
atomics.note: Powers off VMs with vim-cmd, the usual precursor to ESXi disk deletion/encryption (local ART T1529 #15)
